subject: Materials Science
title: Grain Size Engineering
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Grain Size Engineering.

hook.text: A nanocrystalline metal with grains 20 nm across can be five times stronger than the same metal with large grains.

buildup.text: The Hall-Petch equation says yield strength increases as the inverse square root of grain size.

discovery.text: Smaller grains mean more grain boundaries — each boundary stops dislocations from crossing.

twist.text: Below ~10 nm, the trend reverses — grain boundary sliding weakens the material. This is the inverse Hall-Petch effect.

climax.text: Severe plastic deformation techniques like ECAP refine grains to sub-micron sizes for ultra-strong metals.

punchline.text: Control the grain size and you control the strength.

quiz.question: What is the inverse Hall-Petch effect?
options: Strength increases forever as grains shrink
Below a critical grain size, further refinement weakens the material
Larger grains always produce stronger materials
